The house is aware of the fact, as indeed my hon. friend has stated, that last year the Canadian National Railways and the Canadian Pacific railway finally got together in an arrangement to take over all these northern railways, and they are now being operated jointly by the two railway companies through a holding company, the board of directors of which is composed of members drawn equally from each railway. During the past few years, as my hon. friend stated, several surveys of a preliminary character have been undertaken from the Peace River area looking for an outlet down to the coast. So far as my information goes the management of the two railways have not as yet reached any decision as to which of these is the best, and it will be necessary to make the most careful examination in order to establish this. According to the information given me recently, the work will be continued this summer by the railway companies. During the few months that I have been in charge of the department I have discussed the question with the presidents of both railway systems. Naturally they are a little reluctant to give any undertaking to proceed with the work immediately in view of the position of railway revenues at the present time, but so far as I have been able to judge, undoubtedly they are both of opinion that it is only a matter of time until such an outlet will be completed. Of course the terminus of that outlet will depend naturally on the route that is ultimately selected.
My hon. friend made some references to the Hudson Bay railway and drew a parallel between the building of that railway and the progress made in providing an outlet to the Pacific coast from the Peace River country. In that he was supported by my hon. friend from Vancouver South (Mr. Ladner). But the two cases are not exactly parallel. In the first place, the Hudson Bay railway to my certain knowledge has been before the people of western Canada for at least forty years; and
even so far back as 1908 a considerable block of land in the province of Saskatchewan-my hon. friend states there was also some in the province of Alberta, I accept his statement though I have not any personal knowledge of it-I say a very considerable block of land in the province of Saskatchewan was set aside and the proceeds of the sale of those lands were earmarked for the Hudson Bay railway.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Does that mean that we
have to wait forty years too?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I think my hon. friend will not have to wait quite so long as that. The Hudson Bay railway of course was built for the purpose of giving ready access from the central prairie country to tidewater. But may I point out that from the proceeds of the sale of those lands 825,000,000 will be available towards the expense of that undertaking when the collections are finally made. That arrangement was made over twenty years ago and the road will not be finally open for traffic until at least 1931. Let me say, that were it not for the serious position of the railway revenues at the present time, I think there might be very reasonable ground for assuming that the road would be built from the Peace River in the near future.
In his resolution my hon. friend states:
That immediate steps be taken to implement the pledge of the Prime Minister given at Edmonton in November, 1924, with regard to the Peace River outlet.
I am not in a position to say what pledge the Prime Minister gave on that occasion, beyond the information given me by the hon. member, which information, I understand, was taken from a newspaper report.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Could not the Prime
Minister give it? I mailed a copy to him two years ago.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: If my hon. friend by his resolution means that the government should give every attention it can to the carrying out of this undertaking, then I think that his resolution might be accepted. The two railway companies are interested of course in this outlet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Would the hon. gentleman tell me what that means?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The two railway companies are interested in this outlet. So far as the government is concerned I can say that it is prepared to stand behind the Canadian National Railways in the performance of its share of the work, with the necessary funds,

Peace River Railway-Mr. Crerar
that is to say, the government is prepared to provide funds through the customary agency of parliament as in other works carried on by the Canadian National Railways.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Does the minister admit that the government has assumed a real responsibility in the declaration of the Prime Minister of 1924 and 1925?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I did not hear the hon.
gentleman's question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Did not the government assume responsibility in connection with that outlet, or is that responsibility being passed on to the Canadian National Railways?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: No. I am speaking without knowledge of the discussion which took place in parliament on a previous occasion in relation to this subject. I am prepared to say, however, that if my hon. friend who moved the amendment, means that the government should use every agency within its power to secure this outlet, we will accept his resolution at once and without question. I presume that is the meaning my hon. friend wishes to convey, and I can assure him that as far as I am concerned I am prepared to give my very best effort and energy towards the achievement of that purpose. The first essential was the disposal of these Alberta railways. That has been accomplished through the creation of the Alberta Northern railways, and the two major railway companies are now interested in it. They are naturally interested in any outlet to the coast, and so far as the government is concerned I can say that we will use all our influence and will give every assistance we can to the railways to reach a decision at the earliest possible moment so as to have an outlet to the Pacific ocean. I am quite prepared to say that on that understanding the government will accept my hon. friend's resolution.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the closing words of the Minister of Railways (Mr. Crerar) either have a very grave significance or they are merely a repetition of the utterances of the Prime Minister (Mr. Mackenzie King) in 1925 and on subsequent occasions. When a minister of the crown, in particular the Prime Minister, makes statements before the public they are usually taken at their full face value. Undoubtedly the Prime Minister clearly stated in the city of Edmonton that he and his government were deeply concerned with the problems of the settlers and producers in the Peace River district, and that he would see

at the earliest possible moment that they secured an outlet to the Pacific coast. Years have gone by. We had a report in 1925 from a joint board of engineers of the two railways. They were some of the most distinguished men in Canada. On that board were such men as Mr. Sullivan of the Canadian Pacific Railway, Mr. Gzowski, Mr. James, Mr. Hill and some whose signatures are rather difficult to read. These were the most outstanding railway engineers in the country I have in my hand a report which has been in the hands of the government and in possession of both railways. It has been before the railway committee of this house; it has been cited and read, and in it can be found virtually all the information needed in regard to making a decision about the outlets. I say to the Prime Minister that the words which he uttered-'"will use every agency in its power" -are very strong words. I am beginning to wonder if they mean anything, and that is the question my hon. friend has asked in his amendment. We are wondering whether or not the words of the Prime Minister which were uttered five years ago are to be respected, are to be followed out, or are to be implemented with action. I can recall several occasions when my hon. friend the member for Peace River (Mr. Kennedy) brought this matter to the attention of the house. The matter was debated at length and most earnestly in the session of 1927; yet nothing has been done.
Let me bring to the attention of the house one or two points in connection with this matter. The Minister of Railways stated a minute ago that this was undoubtedly a subject of great interest to the people of the Peace River district. It is a subject of great interest to western Canada, and that interest should extend to the whole of Canada. Every member of this house ought to be interested in it. The Peace River district represents a vast empire in the north country. It is not merely a section that is somewhat isolated and in due course will receive consideration, but it is a vast empire, with immense resources, lying at the present time in a more or less idle condition. After the repeated utterances in this house as to the possibilities of that country, it is needless for me to do more than to suggest one or two facts to the government and to this house. Northern British Columbia is west of the most fertile section of the Peace River country. You could put both Norway and Sweden in northern British Columbia north of the Canadian

Peace River Railway-Mr. Stevens
National Railways. They would be placed in a latitude similar to their own, with better conditions and richer resources of minerals, timber and agricultural lands.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
And a much better
climate.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes, a much better climate. In Norway and Sweden there are between nine million and ten million people, whereas in northern British Columbia there are about
20,000	white people-probably there are only about 10,000. I mention these circumstances to show what the possibilities are. In northern Alberta, the coimtry we are discussing, there is a vast area of the finest agricultural land in Canada, with a climate which is exceedingly attractive. To those who understand it, it is not and never has been a question of a few settlers trying to get an outlet for their wheat. I have heard some people say that these settlers had no business to go into that country until transportation facilities had preceded them. As a matter of fact transportation was assured them when the Alberta and Great Waterways Railway was constructed about 1912 or 1913.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Edmonton, Dunvegan and British Columbia Railway.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Yes; when that railway
was undertaken and constructed naturally the settlers expected to receive some consideration. In 1925, in the city of Edmonton, the Prime Minister assured them of an outlet. He was taken at his word, and many more settlers went into the district; there is no question that these settlers had a right to expect consideration. There was no doubt that if the railway were opened to the coast where there would be a reasonable outlet for their products the country would develop by leaps and bounds. The minister says the work of the railways, which at present are looking into the situation, is not yet complete. I submit to him that it is not necessary to sit down and idly wait until these two companies complete their work. He also referred to the financial situation and said that in view of the present financial condition of the Canadian National Railways he did not know whether he would be warranted in going ahead with this project.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not think my hon.
friend quite understood my statement. I said that the two railway companies which were interested in the Alberta Northern railways were rather (reluctant at the moment to undertake this work, in view of the decline in railway revenues.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
In that regard let me say to the minister that in my estimation this is the very time to take up this great national work, if it is justified, because it would take several years to complete this road. This is a big undertaking, and I venture to say that if you started immediately you could not complete the work within two years; indeed, with the use of ordinary methods I doubt if you could construct this road in three or four years. It is a big job, and now is the time to undertake it. We certainly hope that conditions will improve before three or four years pass. To-day we are faced with a good deal! of unemployment, and this would be one way to relieve that situation. This is the time to undertake the work; money is cheap and can be secured to-day probably at much lower rates than may be the case in a year or two.
The main point in the whole matter is that the thing is needed and has been badly needed for years. For several years it has been promised repeatedly, and should be proceeded with. There seems to be a lack of appreciation of the vast heritage which we have in that north country and which this outlet would open up not only to Canada but to the whole world. In view of all these points I think the government should proceed with this work now rather than, in the words of the minister, use every agency under their control in this direction, if in the opinion of the government financial conditions justify it. Let us face the question and say it ought to be done; it is an expenditure which is warranted. The undertaking would not require more than a few million dollars at the outset; probably
82,000,000 would see you through the first year, and the heavy expenditures would come at the end of the second or third years. This work is warranted; conditions are ripe for it; the result's are assured and the undertaking should be proceeded with.
I have just one word more before I conclude. The question of an outlet often has been trotted out as an excuse for not going ahead with the work. Undoubtedly there is a peculiar geographical condition in that country. My hon. friend who represents the district will correct me if I am at all unjust in my statement, but I might tell the house that the Peace River, which runs from the west eastward, goes through a deep cut in the terrain. This cut is of a character which I am assured is impossible of being bridged at any reasonable cost. Therefore the vast area to the north of the river will find an outlet
1798	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Stevens
on the Pacific coast further north than Vancouver. On the other hand there is an area south of the river which naturally would find its outlet through Vancouver.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I am sure my hon. friend from Prince Rupert would not agree with that statement.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I am not so sure of that, but I cannot help it. As a matter of fact I was going to add, for the consolation of those who think there should be only the one outlet, that if that area south of the Peace River and the area now under cultivation, with its adjoining territory, were brought up to full production, these products would tax the full capacity of whatever route was chosen, on a single track basis. There is no doubt of that, and with the two areas separated by nature, as they are by a deep cut, the Peace River district will require two different outlets. There is no question of that in my mind; that is the ultimate outcome, and it is not fair to befuddle the public by putting Prince Rupert or Stewart against Vancouver on the one hand, and Vancouver against the northern points on the other hand. It is not a statesmanlike way to approach the question, and it is not fair. It is not good economics; it is not sound business. The geographical situation is there and it cannot be changed. My opinion is that the government should take the report it has had in its hands for five years and the information gathered since, of which there is a great abundance. Several ministers of the crown have been in that country, and I venture to say there is not one of them who will not endorse the facts I have stated, even if they will not endorse my sentiments. Then there is this other report, which I understand now is complete and which, by the way, is merely the report of a survey of resources. All this information is in the hands of the government, and this work ought to be done. We in this house who are interested in this matter are trying to bring the government to act and not merely indulge in preelection promises. The Minister eschews that, but I rather think that even his immaculate behaviour would not prevent him from wandering slightly astray in making preelection promises. Most people are more or less afflicted with that habit, but there are times when we can very properly say to those who have the reins of power, "You have made certain promises and statements; we believed they were sound and right; the people accepted them seriously and now we call upon you to implement them."

Hon. CHARLES A. DUNNING (Minister of Finance): Mr. Speaker, I desire to say just a few words with reference to a problem with which I had some personal connection during the pakt several years. As I think my hon. friend from Peace River (Mr. Kennedy) knows, personally I regard the question of a western outlet from the Peace River district as Canada's major immediate transportation problem. I use that expression deliberately, having regard to the fact that Canada is just completing the Welland canal, a major undertaking costing a very great deal of money, as well as another transportation effort in the Hudson Bay railway. I say deliberately that in my opinion Canada's major immediate transportation problem is that referred to by my hon. friend in the motion now before the house.
I do not think, Mr. Speaker, that in dealing with this problem the government can be accused of dilatoriness during the past few years. Until a year ago the railways in northern Alberta, the Edmonton, Dunvegan and British Columbia, the Central Canada and the Alberta Great Waterways railways, were owned not by either of our great transportation systems but by the government of the province of Alberta. Negotiations were under way for several years, and finally we were successful dn arranging to have these lines taken over by a company owned jointly by the Canadian National Railways and the Canadian Pacific Railway. The arrangement which was approved by this house one year ago provided for the taking over of the lines and, in addition, for a comprehensive program of branch line construction. I believe I am correct in saying that the two great railway systems which now own the Alberta Northern railways are fulfilling the obligations then undertaken with regard to the construction of branch lines. At that time I indicated to the house that the government was asking the two great railways system to concern themselves immediately with the problem of a western outlet for the system of lines terminating in the Peace River district. That request was made and was pressed upon the railways concerned, not only by myself as Minister of Railways at the time, but also by the Prime Minister, and by my successor in office (Mr. Crerar), who spoke a few moments ago. The hon. member for Vancouver Centre (Mr. Stevens) indicated in his remarks that the work which is being carried on has nothing to do with the finding of a route, but concerns only the resources along the route. I think my hon. friend is confusing two things. The

Peace River Railway-Mr. Dunning
survey of resources in British Columbia now being undertaken by the two great railway corporations has to do with the problem of the Pacific Great Eastern, and is being conducted at the request of and with the cooperation of the government of British Columbia.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Having in mind, of course, the projection of the Pacific Great Eastern into the Peace River country.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Possibly, but not certainly.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Undoubtedly.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend is very sure about that.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend seems certain that the Pacific Great Eastern represents the best outlet to the Pacific coast for the Peace River country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend is not so certain.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: A great many people do not regard the Pacific Great Eastern as a sound economic outlet to the Pacific coast.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I say that that investigation is being carried on primarily to make a survey of the resources on the route of the Pacific Great Eastern and in the territory served by it, and has in mind the projection of that road or the connection of that road with the Peace River country. In explanation of that one observation of mine which the hon. minister has taken up, I had in my hand a moment ago the report of the joint engineers of the railways, Messrs. Sullivan and Gzowski and the other group. In 1925 they reported on the very point which the minister is now discussing, the question of route, the question of outlet, and so forth.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I can continue now to
make my point, that the survey of resources along the route of the Pacific Great Eastern may have and probably will have some bearing upon the settlement of the question of a western outlet, but what was discussed last year in the house, and what we had reference to when we spoke of the government bringing pressure to bear on the railways, had nothing to do with the Pacific Great Eastern. That had to do with an outlet to the Pacific coast from the Peace River country, and the defining by the railway companies of the best, the proper, the most economical, and the soundest route to pursue in that regard without tying up the railway companies either to the Pacific Great Eastern or to any other project.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is quite true.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
As the Minister of Railways has indicated, progress was made last year by the railway companies in this connection. I personally am not satisfied with the progress which has been made, but I think in fairness to the two great railway companies consideration should be given to the serious diminution of revenue which may have dampened their ardour with respect to the surveying of new projects. As my hon. friends from that part of the country know, the Canadian National engineers for years have argued that the Obed route was the best one. I am hoping that that belief may be corrected by the investigations now going on, which are testing that belief as well as the availability and economics of other proposed routes.
As far as my own investigations go, and they are not at all final, I believe that an outlet should be chosen which would make available either of the existing ports on the British Columbia coast. An outlet should be provided which would make it possible for the products of the Peace River country to travel with reasonable economy to either of the ports which now exist on that coast.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Do I understand the
minister to say that the Canadian National is making a survey at the present time on that same basis?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I cannot say what work is going on at the present time.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Was anything done in
1929?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I have been out of touch with things for several months, but my information is that the railways did proceed to gather the information necessary to enable them to make a decision.
The railways may decide that in view of their economic situation they do not desire to go ahead immediately with the building of this road. If that should be the situation, then parliament must take cognizance of that fact. I hesitate to say this, but it may be necessary for parliament to vote directly the funds required for such a project. I had hoped that the economics of the proposal would appeal sufficiently to the great railway companies, who are now in the position of owning the northern lines, 6o that they themselves would propose the measures whereby the work would be definitely undertatken. In that event, parliament would be asked to guarantee the bonds with respect to the Canadian National Railways, and to vote the necessary authority in so far as the northern Alberta railways were concerned.
That is one possibility. Another is that the two railway companies may not agree as to
1800	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Dunning
what should be done. In that event, parliament must be in a position to act, either with the Canadian National Railways or through the power which rests in parliament to undertake matters of this kind if the will of parliament so desires. As a matter of transportation economics, everyone concerned naturally would prefer to see it handled by the railways themselves as a business proposition rather than by any direct governmental undertaking.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: When does the minister expect that the railways will be able to tell him whether or not they will go on with the work?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Minister of Railways has spoken already.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Minister of Finance has arrogated to himself the right of saying that it is up to the railways and that parliamentary responsibility is shelved.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend says that I am arrogating certain things to myself. I was merely telling the house what would be the natural step. If that be arrogance, then I am guilty. However, I do not think I can be accused of arrogance. My hon. friend has a perfect right to speak or to ask me any questions, but I do not think he is treating me quite fairly when he accuses me of arrogance in dealing with a public matter.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I think the hon. gentleman is aware of the difference of the terms "to arrogate" and "arrogance". I repeat that the minister has arrogated to himself the statement of what he claims to be a fact, that the responsibility for the decision in connection with the construction of this line now is upon the railways and not upon parliament.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Oh, no.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The promise of the Prime Minister has been forgotten; the promise of the Minister of Railways has been forgotten-the railways are to decide.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: No.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: When does the hon. minister expect the railways to decide either for or against?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I understand my hon. friend now, but I do not think he understood me. I did not at any time state that the decision rested with the railways. What I did say, and what I intended to convey in the plainest terms, is that it desirable in the

national interests that this undertaking should be carried out if possible in the same manner as any other national transportation undertaking, that is, by the railways concerned, or, failing joint action, by the Canadian National Railways as such. I was giving an assumption of what would happen if the managements of the railways, or the management of the Canadian National Railways acting singly, decided that this proposal could not be recommended to parliament. I hope my hon. friend will listen to me when I say that our position wmuld be then exactly the same as it was in the case of the Hudson Bay railway, because the Canadian National Railways never would and never did assume any responsibility for the construction of that railway.
My hon. friend asks w'hen we may expect an answer from the railways. I think we are entitled to receive very shortly a definite answer from the railway companies concerned. I am not familiar with the recent developments along that line, but I think sufficient time has elapsed to enable the railway companies to make a definite recommendation or a definite statement of their intentions within a very short period. This matter having been evolved so far, having reached the stage where the railways of northern Alberta are owned by the two great railway corporations, having reached the stage where those two railway corporations have had plenty of time -here I am speaking only personally, but I believe they have had plenty of time-to go into the matter thoroughly as to the economics and the shortest route which should be followed, if action is not determined upon by the railways we shall have to face the situation as to whether or not we are in the same position with regard to this matter as we are with regard to the Hudson Bay railway. Personally I have no doubt as to the action we shall take if that is the position in- which we find ourselves.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Supposing the railways
fail to act, what will be the policy of the government?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The policy of the government, the policy of any government, must be to see that the outlet is built.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: When?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My hon. friend realizes
the position in which his question places any minister. Does he want me to give an answer which in effect will be saying to the railway companies:	You have no responsibility in
connection with the matter?

Peace River Railway-Mr. Garland (Bow River)

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The minister made an
answer six years ago.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: What was it?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: That the government would build a railway practically immediately.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend is unfair in that regard, and he knows it better than I do.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The statement is on
Hansard.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The record stands of what this government has accomplished in the face of great difficulty with respect to the Peace River area within the last few years. There is no doubt in my mind that we can have this outlet constructed by normal railway means and to-night I do not want to say anything that would encourage the idea on the part of the railway systems of Canada that they can escape the responsibility which is properly theirs. That is the reason I answer my hon. friend's question in the way I do. But on the other hand I must repeat what I said at the outset, that this to my mind is Canada's major, immediate transportation problem, and that action must be taken with regard to it. Personally I have no fault whatever to find with my hon. friend's resolution as I understand it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I should like to ask the minister a question. He says that this is the immediate responsibility of the two great transcontinental railway companies. I would like to ask the minister:	When this agreement was entered into, did the minister place the onus of an immediate outlet upon those two great transcontinental railway companies?

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The agreement, as my
hon. friend well knows, did not comprehend the question of the outlet at all. I am very much afraid that if any insistence had been placed upon the railways at that time to give a definite undertaking regarding the immediate building of an outlet, we would never have got the agreement; the railways would never have been purchased. As I have stated to the house before, I believe the acquisition of the railway by the Canadian National preferably, or, failing that, by both railways, was a necessary and essential first step in the solving of the problem. Until the railway was in other hands than those of the provincial government I could see no way whereby the problem of an outlet or the development of the Peace River country could be solved. As I have said before-and I say it again to-night-I believe 2419-114
last year's legislation represented a very definite step and the time is now ripe for a further step along the same line.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, may I direct the attention of the house for a moment or two to this question? The present Minister of Finance (Mr. Dunning) on April 13, 1927, made it clear that he regarded it as the absolute duty of the government, of the parliament of Canada, to see that a comprehensive survey was undertaken in order to discover the most economical route for the construction of this line. In 1927 surveys were advocated by the former Minister of Railways, the present Minister of Finance. Surveys were carried on during
1927	and 1928 and there is a partial report based upon the engineers' discoveries or investigations. For 1929, however, we can find no evidence other than the minister's rather hazy statement as to what investigation has been or is being conducted by the Canadian National. It appears to us from the evidence before us that for some reason or another the active work started in 1927 was dropped at the end of 1928, and other than a very vague general statement that the minister believed the Canadian National were conducting an investigation, there is no evidence that they have been so or that they are continuing a survey which they themselves admitted in the
1928	report was only a partial one. If they are not continuing a survey they are trying to carry out a policy on a partial investigation instead of pressing on with the actual survey. That one point alone would indicate to me that there is something lacking in the policy of the government.

speakerposition: Minister of Finance and Receiver General
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: My hon. friend will permit me to answer that question. He surely remembers that the detail work in 1928 was all done north of the Peace River and that very valuable information was secured regarding that area.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
But are the surveys in the various passes continuing? The answer of a man who has given a great deal more study to the question than I have, namely, the hon. member for Peace River (Mr. Kennedy) is: No, they are not continuing with the active surveying. In that report they stated that the surveys therein undertaken were only partial and could by no means be regarded as complete. It looks to me as though for some reason or another all active working connection with this matter, of which the Minister of Finance emphasized the importance, has now stopped, and we have entered what one might call a resting period until the election is over. The engineers who

1802	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Garland (Bow River)
examined the situation and reported in 1924, their report being published in 1927, showed that for the years from 1919 to 1923 the total production of wheat in that area was
5,328,000	bushels and the total production of all grains for the five years was only 19,000.000 bushels, and they indicated that the time for the construction of the road would be when the production of that country reached the
10,000,000 bushel mark. That mark has long been passed; to-day the production of wheat done amounts to 10,000,000 bushels and the total grain production is more than 16,000,000 bushels.
As regards the other point raised by the Minister of Finance, let me point out that the settlement in that district has proceeded and is now proceeding at a far more rapid rate than the branch line program of the two lines can possibly cope with. If ever there was justification for the parliament of Canada stepping in and saying: "Let us get to work on this Peace River outlet," we have it now. Far better to do that if only to relieve the unemployment situation that prevails at present and is likely to continue for some time to come, than to disregard the appeal of those who went into that country-and to-day there are 35,000 people there-believing that the honour of the government was behind the construction of the outlet. They have waited almost too long; they have become disheartened and discouraged, although the hon. member for Peace River has endeavoured to paint a picture of courageous settlers in that district still carrying on the battle against high rates and unfair conditions.
On November 10, 1924, the Prime Minister of Canada, the right hon. gentleman who is now sitting in his seat opposite, definitely stated in the First Presbyterian church in Edmonton-he chose a very excellent place to make the statement-that the construction of the Peace River outlet was an absolute necessity. If it was an absolute necessity in 1924, surely the right hon. gentleman realizes that it is an infinitely greater necessity at this moment, and yet his responsible minister says: This is for the two railway companies to decide, and if the railway companies delay unduly-whatever that may mean-then it will be the duty of this government to step in. That is not a very courageous stand. That is not carrying out pledges or keeping promises. That is not justifying the glorious phrases that the Prime Minister and his colleagues poured forth from the hustings in Vancouver and Calgary and Edmonton. It is not keeping faith with the .people. I ask the Prime Minister now if he will not rise in this house and declare that he recognizes the necessity 
to-day as he did in 1924, and will he not pledge his government to see immediately that this survey is completed at the earliest date and construction commenced as soon as possible; and in order that that may be done, let the necessary vote be inserted in the supplementary estimates.

speakeroldname: Hon. CHARLES STEWART (Minister of the Interior):
speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs; Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Needless to say, Mr. Speaker, there have been two problems in the province of Alberta in which for the past year I have been greatly interested and the solution of which I have tried to forward. While not forgetting the general problems of government I have felt it incumbent upon me to press in season and out of season for the return of the natural resources to the western provinces, and to seek if at all possible a solution of that .problem whereby these resources might be returned. And in conjunction with that problem there was the question of an outlet from this last new great northwest to the Pacific coast.
I very well remember in the days when the Edmonton and Dunvegan railway was being (projected into the Peace River country that I was sent in there for the purpose of making an investigation and bringing in a report to the provincial government on the potentialities of that portion of the province of Alberta. Having visited the territory upon that occasion for the first time, I became convinced that the paramount necessity of the people in that region was to secure a railway, and I so advised the government. The railway was projected into the Peace River country. Sometimes I think, and I believe my views are shared by a great many people, a better route might have been chosen than the one selected. However, the railway is now built and for a considerable number of years the people have been enjoying the facilities afforded by it. The railway, of course, was .projected into the Peace River country with the avowed intention of going on to the coast through some pass. We were told at that time that it would be the Peace River pass. One need only glance at the map to realize that an outlet of that character would best serve the interests of the whole of that territory. Rightly or wrongly I have advocated through all these years the construction of a line through the Peace River pass, giving access either to Prince Rupert, or going south and joining at Fort George with the projected construction of the Pacific Great Eastern to that point in order that the citizens of that territory might have an outlet. This matter was under active discussion in 1923, 1924, 1926 and 1927 prior to the announcement that a complete survey

Peace River Railway-Mr. Stewart (Edmonton)
of these passes was to be made with a view to the selection of the most feasible route, and when that survey was undertaken there was undoubtedly in the minds of the officials of the Canadian National system and of its surveyors the desire and the intention to build from Aggie to Obed on the main line of the Canadian National. I took some responsibility as a representative of Alberta for rather opposing that idea, believing that an outlet should be sought by way of the Peace or Pine pass giving access from that territory over the height of land to the coast and serving, if possible, the two ports of Vancouver and Prince Rupert. I was under the impression that that survey was going on all these years. But last year I understand that the railways made the statement that the most pressing necessity of the moment was the construction of branch lines, and I am somewhat, surprised to know, as stated by my hon. friend, that that survey has not been prosecuted as rapidly as was expected. But I do know this, from the reports of our own Dominion land officers, that down the Peace River there has been a very large number of homesteads located this past year, and one of the immediate necessities, in addition to that mentioned by my hon. friend the Minister of Finance (Mr. Dunning), will be a railroad projected northward to give those people the necessary railway facilities to get their produce to market.
I was also greatly interested in the reported discoveries of minerals along the shores of Slave lake and Great Bear lake. Last year a reconnaissance was made by aeroplane and a very interesting report was brought back as to the possibility of a railway line being projected from some point at or near Grim-shaw northward and northeasterly into the mining area.
So, Mr. Speaker, the problem of railway construction in that country seems to be a very pressing one to say the least, and will continue to be a pressing one. If the railways are undertaking branch line construction, I am convinced that they should also undertake the construction of an outlet to the coast. My hon. friends opposite make the statement that the government themselves should embark upon this project. The Minister of Finance put it very concretely when he stated that if the two railways do not agree it will become the business of the Canadian National Railways to build that outlet, as they have built an outlet to the Hudson bay, to give the people these very greatly needed facilities. Speaking for myself I will continue to advocate as strongly as I can, as I have done in the past, the construction of such an outlet. It was 2419-1141
stated in a letter I believe by Sir Henry Thornton, upon request, when asked what he would consider a reasonable volume of traffic to warrant the building of an outlet for the Peace River country, that when the settlers in that locality produced 10,000,000 bushels of wheat he thought that an outlet to the coast would be warranted. My hon. friend from Peace River (Mr. Kennedy) states that that figure has already been reached.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Sixteen millions bushels.

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs; Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
He, as well
as others, must realize the responsibility of a promise of that kind, and we should have action upon this very greatly needed improvement in that part of the country.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Is the minister aware of any work that is being done at the present time by either or both of the railway companies in connection with the Peace River outlet?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs; Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
So far as
I am concerned, I thought that surveys were being projected. I do know that one season was taken up in reconnaissance work north of the Peace River, and I understood that a complete survey of the Pine pass was to be made. I do know that they have a complete survey of the line to Obeid because I have seen the figures which the engineers have presented as to the cost of construction of that particular line.
May I say that I have not changed my mind? It is not for me to say how the outlet should be built, but I do think that the projection should be westward through one of these passes in order to give the needed facilities, rather than a line from the Edmonton and Dunvegan railway to Obed connecting with the Canadian National line. We must all agree that if the two railway companies can come together about the route to be followed in building the outlet, it will be very much better than having a division of opinion and the necessity of stepping in and constructing the line by the Canadian National Railways alone. I confess frankly that having the two railway companies purchase the existing lines in this territory has not added to the ease of the construction of this outlet.
But may I conclude by saying that so far as I am concerned, and so long as I am a representative of the province of Alberta, I shall continue to advocate just as strenuously as I can the construction of this outlet.

speakeroldname: Hon. R. B. BENNETT (Leader of the Opposition):
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the motion before
1801	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Bennett
the house is the usual motion that the Speaker do now leave the chair. The amendment thereto calls upon the Prime Minister (Mr. Mackenzie King) to implement a promise which he made to the people of Canada. The discussion has wandered far afield and has covered many matters which were not involved in the observations made by the hon. gentleman (Mr. Kennedy) who moved the amendment.
Should the Prime Minister of this country make a promise on the eve of an election for the purpose of securing support for his candidate and then disregard that promise? That is the question; nothing more nor less than that. It is all right to go to Saskatoon and ask how many miles of branch lines you have to build to get support for the member. It is all right to think in terms of miles of railroad, as was done by the Prime Minister in the reported speech at Saskatoon, and it is all right to go to Edmonton and promise a Peace River outlet at the earliest possible moment, and it is all right to make that statement again in Vancouver. But Sir Wilfrid Laurier once said that chickens have a habit of coming home to roost. And they have come home to roost in this case! What is the Prime Minister going to say about it? That is the question.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Nothing.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It is not what the Minister of the Interior (Mr. Stewart) says about the painful struggles he has made for Alberta and the weeping he has indulged in during the past year in the intervals when he had something more to think about than natural resources. But had he been thinking of the natural resources during the past six years we would not have been taking up the time of the house this session in doing tardy justice to the western provinces. It is not enough for the Minister of Railways (Mr. Crerar) to say there will not be a Peace River outlet for a year or two. That is not an answer to the question before this house to-night. The question now before the house involves the honour of parliament and the honour of the Prime Minister. It is not good enough for the Minister of Finance (Mr. Dunning) to tell us that he knows something about this thing and to work himself up into a fine frenzy as to what he has done to make the government live up to its promises. What is the answer that this parliament and the people of Canada are waiting for? Shall we tolerate such a condition of affairs in this country that the Prime Minister, with all the authority and responsibility of a minister of the crown,
fMr. Bennett.]
goes out to the trusting people and standing before them in a church edifice at Edmonton tells them what he will do, and then three or four years later still disregards that promise? That is the issue involved in the amendment made by the hon. member for Peace River. It is high time such an amendment was made in this house. It is high time for the people of this country to realize that they cannot be longer deluded by these promises made by the Prime Minister on the eve of an election. It is only a few days ago that the same sort of thing had to be dealt with. When one reads the language used by the right hon. gentleman in Vancouver one realizes that it was a promise as near as he could make a promise and yet not make one, following upon the fact that he had made the promise at Edmonton and was confronted with it at Vancouver. But it was good enough to try to mislead three thousand people or more. Where is the honour of this government? They prate and prattle of the high moral issues that are involved, in a fine frenzy they talk about the ideals of Liberalism and the open road. But let them keep their promises; then we will have some honour in this country. It is all right for you to promise branch lines when by so doing you can get votes; but when that day is past you come and tell parliament, "We have not anything to do with branch lines; it belongs to the railways." Read the speeches made by the right hon. gentleman while in western Canada within the last fifteen months in which he took credit for what his government had done in constructing branch railways. After all, who is able to build these railways, the government or the railway companies? Some people have thought that this government endeavoured to control the railway companies. Most people looked upon the speech made by the right hon. gentleman as an indication of that. Sir, I put to the house this question: If the government has power enough to build branch lines, or to compel the railway companies to do so, it surely has power enough to protect the honour of parliament and the honour of the Prime Minister. That is the question at issue. Upon that question I will not permit the hon. gentleman, even if he desires, to withdraw his motion. I think it is high time this parliament passed upon the observations made by the right hon. Prime Minister. The people of this country, to use the language of the street, are beginning to understand the game, they are beginning to see through it, they are beginning to strip this mantle of righteousness that the right hon. gentleman wears, realizing the time is come when promises given for votes must

Peace, River Railway-Mr. Bennett
be implemented in parliament or else he must cease to hold office. That is the position in respect to it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I just wish to say that
I had no intention of withdrawing the motion.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I felt pretty certain of
that, but I wished so to intimate to my hon. friend beforehand so he would not make any mistake about it. But there is the issue, sir, the whole issue, and it could not be made clearer. The Prime Minister went to the trusting and confiding electors of Brandon and promised them what he would do; then three or four years afterwards, as the hon. member says, he pleads that he is in the hands of the railways. The matter was in the hands of the railways then, or else we have been deceived ; one or the other. Either the railways were free to do as they pleased with respect to branch lines, or they were not; and if they were not, the government would be able to claim credit for its branch lines program. Indeed, at the time it said: "Look at the trouble we had with the Senate when our branch line legislation reached that chamber." Now the Senate is reformed by the advent there of the former Minister of Immigration (Mr. Forke)-and all is well.
Now, sir, I ask, Does the Minister of the Interior think the people of Alberta are deceived with that sort of talk?

speakerposition: Minister of Immigration and Colonization; Superintendent-General of Indian Affairs; Minister of Mines; Minister of the Interior
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Oh, no.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Of course, he does not
think so. He knows the electors of Edmonton will recall the speech made by the Prime Minister in the Presbyterian church, he knows their memories have not entirely failed them, and he knows they will hold not only the Prime Minister but himself responsible for the failure to implement that promise. The Minister of Finance is absent. No wonder! He came in and did his little bit; he has been a boy scout for to-day; he has done one good deed. He has come up and tried to defend the breach of honour and of obligation by the Prime Minister to the people of Canada, especially of western Canada. Having done so he has gone out. He will get the meritorious reward for service well done. As I have said, he has been a good boy scout to-day, he has done one good turn-he has helped a big brother.
But, sir, some hon. gentlemen look upon these matters as what they call "just the pastime of politics." They think it is a delightful thing to make these promises before an election and then say, "Look how we outdid the Conservatives." Mr. Meighen could
not make such promises and implement them, for he was not in power. Oh, no. But when he made a promise he kept it.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Oh, oh.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Of course it would be
so strange to hon. gentlemen opposite to think that any leader of a party would keep a promise that they laugh. Why would they not? Long habit has induced them to believe that when a prime minister makes a promise he has no intention of keeping it. They laugh at the very thought of a prime minister keeping his promise. Is it any wonder they laugh? If I sat behind the Prime Minister I would certainly feel like laughing. Why, even the Minister of Justice laughs at the thought. And may I add that the performances in this house during the last three or four months are strictly in keeping with the same general principle? I will review them at a later date, but I shall nol do it now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: To-morrow?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
To-morrow? Well, that
would be a very opportune time. I thank the Roderick for the word; it steels my sword. Now, let us recall the circumstance in connection with the Peace River outlet.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Before my hon. friend
goes on, may I tell him why we laugh?

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Well, I would judge that it was because of the recent appointment to the bench in Quebec; I would judge that from remarks my hon. friend has made on previous occasions.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I will tell my hon. friend why his friends cheer. It was because he, the new judge, was a member of an administration the premier of which, Mr. Taschereau, is the greatest Tory in this country, according to the leader of the opposition; he took the crown off his head to put it on the head of the Quebec premier. I will tell my hon. friend why we laughed. We laughed because the present leader of the opposition presented a petition on behalf of a man named Collins to unseat the present member for Peace River.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Now, my friend from
Temiscouata who has such a high regard for judicial authorities-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: It is a precedent that does n-ot date back to the reign of Queen Anne.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
It was in the reign of
Queen Anne of happy memory that a statute was passed and the decision of the privy
1806	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Bennett
council made with respect to the meaning of the words trade and commerce. Perhaps the hon. gentleman could apply those words in connection with the appointment to which he refers.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I do not know if there is a trade between the leader of the opposition and the hon. member for Peace River-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I can assure the hon.
member that there is no commerce.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Then it is "peace" river.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
There should always be
peace, perfect peace, between the hon. gentleman and myself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Then it is the styx.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Peace River project is a matter upon which we voted in this house. The government of the day was not only content to make observations but the Prime Minister induced his followers to vote down the resolution moved at that time by the hon. member (Mr. Kennedy). I supported the motion, believing that the time had come when it was desirable that a little progress should be made. There are those yonder who say that there is no progress in the Conservative party, that progress rests entirely with Liberalism. For instance, there is the chief whip of the Liberal party, who is the champion of that statement. I have been reading some of his magnificent speeches delivered throughout the various parts of Ontario and Quebec; he speaks in Ontario chiefly. In his opinion progress is synonymous with Liberalism-but progress may be backward; you may slip down hill as well as up hill.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is Conservatism.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: No. Tennyson expressed it very well when he said, that man's the best conservative that lops the mouldered branch away. I would judge that that is why the hon. member for Temiscouata complains of the Prime Minister's recent appointment to the Quebec bench. It is all right now, is it?

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I think so.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Very well, it is all fixed up now.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: And I have nothing to withdraw.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: There is not so much peace after all; the hon. gentleman says he has nothing to withdraw. His observations the other day indicated that the gentleman appointed was unfit for the position, but now he says he has nothing to withdraw. I shall leave it to the minister and his supporters.

speakerposition: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: That is the opinion of the hon. gentleman himself.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Let us look at the Peace River outlet which has been endorsed as the policy of the Prime Minister. I have before me the headlines of the speech made by the Prime Minister on November 6, 1929.
Peace River Outlet Endorsed as Policy by Prime Minister.
Vancouver Audience hears Premier King's Assurance That His Government Will Cheek all "Dilly-dallying" In Decision on Survey.
While his government was dilly-dallying and while his Minister of the Interior was inactive, the survey stopped. The survey having stopped the dilly-dallying continued.
I can only repeat the question: Can we hope to make progress in Canada if the chief citizen of the country makes promises on the hustings and in parliament, secures the support, and then makes no attempt to fulfil them? In this case the surveyors are withdrawn, the railway is not completed, and the outlet is undiscovered; progress is backward as well as forward. The speech of the right hon. gentleman remains unredeemed, and the obligation is disregarded six years afterwards. That is the position I put to this house; and I shall observe with much amusement the attitude of my hon. friends when they attempt to condone the action of their Prime Minister. They will no doubt as usual take their whippings like litttle men, realizing that they have done one more good turn for the cause which they supported.

speakeroldname: Right Hon. W. L. MACKENZIE KING (Prime Minister):
speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, the hon.
leader of the opposition during the course of his remarks said something about wandering far afield. At that time he was referring to other speakers, but I think his remarks would more often apply to his own address. My hon. friend has said that we have before us an amendment to the motion to go into supply, and he asked what the action and comment of the Prime Minister will be in connection with that amendment. He then turned to his friend from Peace River district who moved the amendment and made the statement that he does not propose to allow him to withdraw the amendment.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: No, I did not say that.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Oh, yes.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I said I would not permit him to withdraw it without first taking a vote.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The hon.
gentleman said that he would not permit the hon. member for Peace River to withdraw his motion without first having a vote taken. The

Peace River Railway-Mr. Mackenzie King
hon. member for Peace River then, doing his part, told us that he did not intend to allow the amendment to be withdrawn.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: I have not heard anything yet that prompts me to withdraw it.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
My hon. friend will not need to withdraw his amendment because the government is prepared to accept it; the government does not propose to have the amendment used simply for political purposes. Let me read the amendment that we may see the extent to which hon. gentlemen are trying to play politics with this important Peace River project. Listen to the amendment; it reads as follows:
That immediate steps be taken to implement the pledge of the Prime Minister given at Edmonton in November, 1924, with regard to the Peace River outlet.
Do hon. gentleman opposite expect that hon. members on this side of the house are going to vote not to implement any pledge given by the Prime Minister? If hon. gentlemen opposite do not expect them to vote in that way what does my hon. friend mean when he says he will not allow this amendment to be withdrawn on the government giving an undertaking that it is prepared to carry out its undertaking? The amendment has been so worded and introduced as an amendment on going into supply as to place the government before the people of this country as appearing to be in the position of. declining to implement a pledge which the amendment says has been given by the Prime Minister. I tell my hon. friend-

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Six years ago.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not care
whether it was six or sixty years ago so long as the pledge remains, and so long as there has been good and substantial reasons why it could not have been implemented sooner. I am sure the reasons which have governed up to the present will be supported by public opinion. I am prepared to say that when the opportunity presents itself for the carrying out of this pledge, it will be carried out. I do not propose to have hon. members on this side of the house put in the false position of appearing to be voting for anything to the contrary. If hon. gentlemen opposite between them wish to draft an amendment with a view ' to trving to embarrass the government politically, that is their own lookout, but I can tell the people of this country and particularly the people of western Canada that as far as this Peace River outlet is concerned, the government does not believe that tactics of the kind will help the project. The government is in earnest with respect to having that route
constructed just as soon as, having regard for essential consideration, may be possible. If hon. gentlemen opposite are determined to seek to make political capital out of it they will have to make their own explanations to the electors.
My hon. friend says a pledge was made in 1924 at Edmonton, and he reads words which he indicates are those directly spoken by myself. To begin with, I do not think the report has anything in direct quotations. It is a statement of what I purported to say at the time I was speaking in Edmonton.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
The important part of
the speech is in direct quotations, and it was taken from the Edmonton Bulletin, a friendly newspaper.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
I do not think I used the expression "I pledge myself" in regard to anything; I am quite sure that is not my own language. If I had been speaking with respect to an undertaking of the government I would have made a reference to the government and said that I spoke in the name of the government. I think I am sufficiently well acquainted with my own manner of speaking to know the language I would have used at the time, and in giving any undertaking for the government, I would have taken care to mention the government in that way.
However, I have not the slightest doubt that I did say I believed the construction of this route was essential and necessary and that it would be undertaken-apparently the word "humanly" was used-as soon as would be humanly possible. That is general language; it does not mean that the railroad necessarily would be constructed that year or the year following. It meant that the road would be constructed, having regard to those circumstances for which a government must have regard, as soon as relevant circumstances would make such construction possible.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: When will that time be?

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
If my hon. friend will wait a moment I will tell him. At the lime I was speaking, conditions were very different from what conditions are to-day with respect to the possibility of the government being in a position to guarantee the passage of measures through this parliament. Reference has been made also to a speech which I delivered in Vancouver, during the course of which I am reported to have said that we had had our experience with regard to branch lines, and so we had. When I was speaking in Edmonton, I am not at all sure that that was not at a time a program of branch line construction which we had placed
1808	COMMONS
Peace River Railway-Mr. Mackenzie King
before parliament and which had passed this house had been rejected by the other house. If I am not mistaken our branch line programs were thrown out on two or three different occasions. That being the case I think I was justified, speaking in Edmonton in qualifying my language as to what in the name of the government I could undertake with respect to a railway which would afford an outlet from the Peace district to the Pacific. The report of my speech as read says that they would have to be patient.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: The Prime Minister was discussing the Hudson Bay railway and the Peace River outlet.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: Yes, I was discussing the Hudson Bay railway and the Peace River outlet, but I was discussing these questions at a time when I knew the extent of the government's power in the matter of getting railway legislation through this parliament and I was speaking in the light of that knowledge. When I spoke at Vancouver, I was equally careful to have regard to what I believed the power of the government would be with reference to legislation which it would wish to have enacted by this parliament. I was careful not to make unconditional promises, but to make perfectly clear to the electorate difficulties with which in the past the government had been forced to contend and difficulties with which we might have to contend in the future. My hon. friends opposite have read, from the Vancouver Province of November 16, 1929, headlines which appeared above the article dealing with the meeting which was held in that city.

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext: And the context as well.

speakerposition: Prime Minister; President of the Privy Council; Secretary of State for External Affairs
maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
speechtext:
But not all the context; I am going to show that my hon. friends picked out parts of the context as best suited their purpose. I will show also what they did not read. This was the heading:
Peace River Outlet Endorsed As Policy by Prime Minister.
Vancouver Audience Hears Premier King's Assurance That His Government Will Check All "Dilly-Dallying" in Decision on Survey.
Then my hon. friend read some of the text, as follows:
"As a government we believe in the Pacific outlet for the Peace," said the Premier, ''and we don't intend to allow the railways to dillydally m reaching their decision. If they do then the authority of the state can be called on to make them reach one."

maintopic: SUPPLY-PEACE RIVER RAILWAY OUTLET AMENDMENT TO MOTION OF MINISTER OF FINANCE FOR COMMITTEE
